fot_token_is_dispute_token.meaning: the configured disputeToken is a fee-on-transfer token

dispute_amount_sent_tokens.meaning: disputeAmount tokens sent by the user in disputeTree()

deposit_fee_tokens.meaning: transfer fee deducted by the fee-on-transfer token on the deposit

no_recovery_path_available.meaning: no recovery path exists: recoverERC20() requires resolveDispute() to succeed first and further deposits do not help because the FoT token takes fees on outgoing transfers

resolve_dispute_completed.meaning: resolveDispute() completes successfully (returning stake to disputer or slashing to governor) and clears the disputer state

tree_updates_blocked_observed.meaning: no new Merkle trees can be published and tree revocation is blocked, freezing claims on stale lastTree data

assumptions: The disputeTree deposit and the resolveDispute attempt are treated as separate steps; the deposit is prior state.
The scenario is legitimate protocol use by the governor and an honest disputer; no unauthorized caller is involved.
The 1% fee example (10 of 1000 tokens) is illustrative of the fee-on-transfer behavior, not a fixed protocol constant.

unresolved.description: Report does not specify the exact FoT fee percentage applied to the resolution transfer, only that a fee is burned first; the resolution-transfer fee amount is not bound.
Report does not state whether the deposit and the resolveDispute attempt occur in the same or separate transactions.

limitations: The impact tree_updates_blocked is a downstream consequence of resolveDispute() always reverting; the plan encodes it as the forbidden observable in the relation rather than as a precondition.
The fee-on-transfer fee is represented by the report's illustrative 10-of-1000 example; the actual resolution-transfer fee is left to code binding.
Tree revocation being blocked is folded into tree_updates_blocked per the report's ambiguity note.
